Bootstrap for Regularised Partial Correlation Networks

Source: R/boot_glasso.R
boot_glasso.Rd

boot_glasso() assesses how accurately an EBIC graphical lasso network is estimated and how stable its centralities are, by resampling the observations (Epskamp, Borsboom & Fried, 2018). One call runs a nonparametric bootstrap, which gives percentile intervals and inclusion probabilities for every edge, intervals for each node's centralities and predictability, and bootstrap tests of the difference between every pair of edges and every pair of nodes; and a case-dropping bootstrap, which gives each centrality measure's correlation-stability (CS) coefficient. It takes the raw data or a network built with method = "glasso".

An interval shows how precisely an edge weight is estimated: a wide one means the weight changes a good deal between samples. Epskamp et al. (2018) caution that, because the lasso shrinks estimates towards zero, these intervals are not tests of whether an edge differs from zero; the thresholded network (edges whose interval excludes zero) and the "significant" count in print() read them that way, and the inclusion probability (how often an edge is non-zero across resamples) is a separate summary. The CS-coefficient is the largest proportion of cases that can be dropped while more than 95% of the subsamples keep a correlation above 0.7 with the original centralities; Epskamp et al. (2018) suggest it should not be below 0.25 and preferably above 0.5 before the centrality order is interpreted, and print() labels the values accordingly. The difference tests are not corrected for the number of pairs compared.

Usage

boot_glasso(
  x,
  iter = 1000L,
  cs_iter = 500L,
  cs_drop = seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1),
  alpha = 0.05,
  gamma = 0.5,
  nlambda = 100L,
  centrality = c("strength", "expected_influence", "betweenness", "closeness"),
  centrality_fn = NULL,
  cor_method = "pearson",
  ncores = 1L,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'boot_glasso'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'boot_glasso'
summary(object, type = "edges", ...)

# S3 method for class 'boot_glasso'
plot(x, type = "edges", measure = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

The data: a data frame or numeric matrix with one row per observation and one column per variable, cleaned as in build_glasso(): non-numeric columns and a column named rid are set aside; columns with non-syntactic names, all-missing and constant columns, and rows with a missing value are dropped, each with a message; fewer than 2 variables or 3 complete rows raise an error. A square symmetric matrix with matching row and column names is read as a correlation or covariance matrix and refused (class nestimate_bad_input): it has no observations to resample. Or a netobject (or cograph_network) built with method = "glasso", whose data are resampled; any gamma, nlambda or cor_method set in its params replaces the arguments of the same name, and its lambda.min.ratio, penalize.diagonal and refit are used too, so original_pcor is the network's weights. Any other network raises an error. A correlation or covariance matrix is not accepted: a matrix is always read as data, its rows as observations. For the print() and plot() methods: a boot_glasso.

iter

The number of nonparametric bootstrap resamples, at least 2. Default 1000.

cs_iter

The total number of case-dropping iterations, at least 1. Default 500. As in bootnet, each iteration draws one proportion from cs_drop at random, so the iterations are spread across the proportions (about cs_iter / length(cs_drop) each) rather than repeated cs_iter times at each one.

cs_drop

The proportions of cases to drop, each in (0, 1). Default seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1).

alpha

The significance level: the intervals run from the alpha / 2 to the 1 - alpha / 2 quantile, and print() and the "edge_diff" / "centrality_diff" plots mark the difference tests' p-values below it as differing. Default 0.05.

gamma

The EBIC hyperparameter; larger values give sparser networks. Default 0.5. Replaced by the value stored in a netobject.

nlambda

The number of lambda values in the regularisation path, at least 2. Default 100. Replaced by the value stored in a netobject.

centrality

The centrality measures to compute. Default all four built-in ones: "strength" (sum of absolute edge weights), "expected_influence" (sum of signed edge weights), "betweenness" and "closeness" (on shortest paths with distance 1 / |weight|). Without centrality_fn, names may be abbreviated. Any other name needs centrality_fn, which then computes it; the built-in measures are always computed internally.

centrality_fn

A function for measures beyond the four built-in ones: it is called as centrality_fn(mat) on the partial correlation matrix and returns a named list of centrality vectors, such as list(my_metric = ...). Default NULL; a measure in centrality that is neither built in nor returned by it raises an error.

cor_method

The correlation method: "pearson" (default), "spearman" or "kendall". Replaced by the value stored in a netobject.

ncores

The number of cores for the resampling, used through parallel::mclapply(), which forks the R process; on Windows it accepts only 1, and any larger value raises an error. Default 1 (sequential).

seed

A seed for reproducible resampling; the session's random state is restored when the call returns. Default NULL uses the current random stream. With ncores > 1 the resamples are reproducible only under RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG").

...

For the plot() method with type = "edge_diff" or "centrality_diff": order, "sample" (default) to sort the edges by their absolute weight or the nodes by their centrality, or "id" to sort them alphabetically; with type = "edge_diff" also pos_color and neg_color, the fills for a cell where the edge on the x-axis has a larger or a smaller mean bootstrap weight than the edge on the y-axis (defaults "#C0392B" and "#2C6E8A"). Ignored otherwise, and by the print() and summary() methods.

object

For the summary() method: a boot_glasso.

type

What to return or draw. For the summary() method: "edges" (default), the edge intervals sorted by decreasing absolute weight; "centrality", the centrality intervals; "cs", the case-dropping table; "predictability", the predictability intervals; or "all", the four together. For the plot() method: "edges" (default), each edge's weight and interval; "stability", the mean correlation with the original centralities against the proportion dropped, with a dashed line at 0.7; "edge_diff", a heatmap of the mean bootstrap difference between every pair of edges, faint where the pair does not differ at alpha and starred where it does, with the edge weights on the diagonal; "centrality_diff", a heatmap of which node pairs differ on measure, with the node values on the diagonal; or "inclusion", each edge's inclusion probability, with a dashed line at 0.5.

measure

For the plot() method with type = "centrality_diff": the centrality measure to compare, one of those computed (names may be abbreviated). Default NULL, the first measure computed.

Value

A boot_glasso object. print() reports the data size, alpha and gamma, the number of edges whose interval excludes zero, the mean inclusion probability, the failed resamples when there are any, each measure's CS-coefficient with its label, the number of edge pairs that differ, and the timing; summary() returns the table chosen by type (edges, centralities, case-dropping results or predictability; described at the end of this section); plot() draws one figure chosen by type. The object's fields:

original_pcor

The partial correlation matrix of the original data.

original_precision

The precision matrix of the original data.

original_centrality

A named list with one vector of node values per centrality measure.

original_predictability

A named vector of each node's R-squared.

edge_ci

A data frame with one row per edge: edge, weight, ci_lower, ci_upper and inclusion.

edge_inclusion

A named vector of edge inclusion probabilities.

thresholded_pcor

The partial correlation matrix with every edge whose interval includes zero set to zero.

centrality_ci

A named list with one data frame per centrality measure: node, value, ci_lower, ci_upper.

cs_coefficient

A named vector with the CS-coefficient of each centrality measure.

cs_data

A data frame of the case-dropping results, one row per drop proportion and measure: drop_prop, measure, mean_cor, prop_above (the share of that proportion's iterations correlating above 0.7) and n_samples (the iterations that drew that proportion).

edge_diff_p

A symmetric matrix of the edge-difference p-values; NULL when the network has more than 500 edges.

centrality_diff_p

A named list with one symmetric matrix of node-difference p-values per centrality measure.

predictability_ci

A data frame with one row per node: node, r2, ci_lower, ci_upper.

boot_edges

An iter x edges matrix of the bootstrap edge weights.

boot_centrality

A named list with one iter x nodes matrix of bootstrap values per centrality measure.

boot_predictability

An iter x nodes matrix of bootstrap R-squared values.

nodes

The node names.

n

The sample size.

p

The number of variables.

iter, cs_iter, cs_drop, alpha, gamma, nlambda

The settings used.

centrality_measures

The centrality measures computed.

cor_method

The correlation method used.

lambda_path

The lambda path used for every fit.

lambda_selected

The lambda selected on the original data.

n_failed, cs_n_failed

The numbers of bootstrap and case-dropping resamples whose estimation failed and that were left out.

timing

A named vector of elapsed seconds: total, phase1 (the original fit), bootstrap, case_drop and statistics.

print() returns its input invisibly. summary() returns a data frame: for type = "edges" the edge_ci table (edge, weight, ci_lower, ci_upper, inclusion) sorted by decreasing absolute weight, for "cs" the cs_data table and for "predictability" the predictability_ci table; "centrality" returns a named list with one data frame per measure (node, value, ci_lower, ci_upper), and "all" a named list of the four (edges, centrality, cs, predictability). plot() returns a ggplot object, which is drawn when the call is made at the top level. The edge-difference plot raises an error when the test was skipped (more than 500 edges).

Details

The network is estimated as build_glasso() estimates it: with a netobject, with its own params (lambda.min.ratio, penalize.diagonal, refit); with data, with that function's defaults (smallest lambda 0.01 times the largest, no penalty on the diagonal, the selected penalty re-solved exactly, no unregularised refit). The lambda path is set once from the original data and reused for every resample, which is fitted with the same settings; the penalty is chosen on it by EBIC with gamma. Strength is the sum of a node's absolute edge weights and expected influence the sum of its signed weights; betweenness and closeness use shortest paths with distance 1 / |weight|, computed without igraph. Predictability is \(1 - 1 / \Theta_{ii}\), from the diagonal of the precision matrix, bounded to 0–1.

The case-dropping bootstrap follows bootnet: each of the cs_iter iterations draws one proportion from cs_drop at random, keeps that share of the rows (at least p + 1 of them) without replacement, and correlates the subsample's centralities with the original ones; a centrality that is constant across nodes counts as a correlation of 0. The difference tests give, for each pair, the two-sided bootstrap p-value 2 * min(P(d >= 0), P(d <= 0)) of the difference d between the two edges or nodes, capped at 1, with ties counted in both tails. The edge-difference test is skipped for networks with more than 500 edges. A resample whose estimation fails (for example, a variable constant in the resample) is kept as missing and left out of the intervals and the case-dropping results; the failures are counted in n_failed and cs_n_failed, shown by print(), and reported in a warning of class nestimate_resample_failed. The function was written as a faster, single-call alternative to running bootnet several times.

Methods

  • plot() draws one figure of the bootstrap results per call, chosen with type.

References

Epskamp, S., Borsboom, D., & Fried, E. I. (2018). Estimating psychological networks and their accuracy: A tutorial paper. Behavior Research Methods 50(1), 195-212. doi:10.3758/s13428-017-0862-1 (source of the CS-coefficient and of the case-dropping, edge-difference and centrality-difference procedures reproduced here.)

See also

build_network, bootstrap_network

Examples

set.seed(1)
dat <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(60), ncol = 3))
net <- build_network(dat, method = "glasso")
bg <- boot_glasso(net, iter = 10, cs_iter = 5, centrality = "strength")
# \donttest{
set.seed(42)
mat <- matrix(rnorm(60), ncol = 4)
colnames(mat) <- LETTERS[1:4]
net <- build_network(as.data.frame(mat), method = "glasso")
# iter = 20 keeps the example fast; a real analysis uses 1000 or more.
boot <- boot_glasso(net, iter = 20, cs_iter = 10, seed = 42,
  centrality = c("strength", "expected_influence"))
print(boot)
#> GLASSO Bootstrap (20 iterations, 10 case-drop per proportion)
#>   Data: 15 x 4  |  Alpha: 0.05  |  Gamma: 0.50
#>   Edges: 0/6 significant (CI excludes zero)
#>   Mean inclusion probability: 0.34
#> 
#>   Centrality Stability (CS-coefficient):
#>     strength:              0.00 [Unstable]
#>     expected_influence:    0.00 [Unstable]
#> 
#>   Edge differences: 0/15 pairs significantly different
#>   Timing: 1.1s (bootstrap: 0.7s, case-drop: 0.4s)
summary(boot, type = "edges")
#>     edge weight    ci_lower  ci_upper inclusion
#> 1 A -- B      0 -0.11158199 0.2237159      0.35
#> 2 A -- C      0 -0.35185567 0.0000000      0.45
#> 3 B -- C      0 -0.30946900 0.2065199      0.25
#> 4 A -- D      0  0.00000000 0.3570903      0.50
#> 5 B -- D      0 -0.15048304 0.3105727      0.35
#> 6 C -- D      0 -0.03724162 0.1787669      0.15
# }
